intro: Interpreting builds listening, judgment and the ability to explain meaning across cultures. The closest of the 25 careers below is teaching adult basic education and English as a second language, with an 80% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $61,540, about 2% more than the $60,170 interpreters and translators earn.
why_it_works: Every assignment asks you to grasp what someone means, choose the right words fast and stay neutral under pressure. O*NET rates judgment, service orientation and social perceptiveness at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Language teaching, speech-language work and compliance roles use those strengths. Most matches need no new degree. The skills to build are analyzing systems, teaching groups and coordinating projects.
tips: Teach an evening ESL class or tutor online to test whether classroom work suits you.
Compliance Officers earn $80,730, which is 34% more, and value careful reading of rules and documents.
List your language pairs, certifications and subject areas, such as legal or medical, on every application.

faq.q: What jobs can former interpreters and translators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are adult education and ESL instructors (80%), secondary school teachers (76%) and Speech-Language Pathologists (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Secondary teachers earn $72,040, which is 20% more than the $60,170 median for interpreters and translators, though most states require a teaching license.

faq.q: Which careers for interpreters pay more?
faq.a: 19 of the 25 matches pay more than interpreting. Speech-Language Pathologists earn $97,870 (63% more), Compliance Officers $80,730 (34% more) and postsecondary foreign language teachers $79,350 (32% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Speech-language pathology usually requires a graduate degree and a license.

faq.q: Do interpreters need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: Often not. 19 of the 25 matches need no more education than interpreters already have, but 6 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 41% of workers in the closest match, so your language degree may already be enough.

faq.q: What skills should interpreters and translators build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are systems analysis, instructing, systems evaluation and coordination. Complex problem solving already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so teaching groups and working with systems and data are the main steps for most moves.
